text: - [LLOG.2.5] Retracted only when the **last** justification goes away.

idris.name: llog_2_5__reach_engine_well_founded
idris.note: Over the surviving inputs, the well-founded answer for the engine's own table retracts both Reach facts -- what this clause intends and the refcount does not do.

idris.name: llog_2_5__boundary_unfounded
idris.note: AT A BOUNDARY the well-founded facts are live, and if any live fact is not well-founded, the live facts outside the well-founded set are an unfounded set -- what recompute-and-diff at the boundary would retract, and what the refcount keeps.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_after_exact
idris.note: For any list retracted that holds no well-founded id and every live id outside the well-founded set, the live ids after are exactly the well-founded set.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_exact
idris.note: THE STEP IS EXACT. After recompute-and-diff the live facts are exactly the well-founded set of the engine's table over the live facts before: this clause with "the last justification" read as the last grounded one, the reading that is the contract. On a positive program, from a state satisfying the run invariant; no clause states the step.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_gone_greatest
idris.note: And it holds every unfounded set among the live facts: the diff is the greatest unfounded set, no more retracted than must be and no unfounded support left.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_gone_unfounded
idris.note: What the step retracts is an unfounded set among the live facts, whenever it retracts anything: no base fact is in it, and every justification of a member with live antecedents uses another member.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_reach_engine
idris.note: Executed: on Lcyc/TmsWitnesses.idr's reach run, where the refcount leaves both Reach facts live on each other alone, the step retracts both and leaves the two edges with every table empty.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_grow
idris.note: The well-founded set survives the step's own bookkeeping: the rows the cascade keeps still ground every surviving fact. What makes one step suffice.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_in_cascade_of
idris.note: The refcount cascade never retracts a well-founded fact, even over the smaller live set a recompute-and-diff retraction leaves: what makes the step's cascade retract nothing more.

idris.name: Llog_2_5__grounded
idris.note: Every live fact is in the well-founded set of the state's own table over its live facts: each has a justification grounded in the facts nothing justifies.

idris.name: Llog_2_5__grounded_s
idris.note: The same, of a state.

idris.name: llog_2_5__grounded_empty
idris.note: With an empty table every live fact is base, so grounded: the start of a run.

idris.name: llog_2_5__rd_run_grounded
idris.note: AT EVERY STATE OF EVERY RUN of Rete/RecomputeFire.idr's engine -- recompute-and-diff after every action, which no clause states -- from an input with unique ids, the run invariant holds and every live fact is grounded, including after a rule's withdraw mid-pump, where the refcount engine keeps an unfounded closure live (Main.idr's alarm trace). Positive programs.

idris.name: Llog_2_5__stratified_list
idris.note: Strata in the SCC-DAG's order: no stratum reads what any later one derives.

idris.name: llog_2_5__all_strata
idris.note: All the strata's justifications, first stratum first, by structure.

idris.name: llog_2_5__hybrid_agrees
idris.note: Stratum by stratum, the hybrid agrees with the recompute from a base with the same members in the universe, when the recompute's facts are live: a recursive stratum is a recompute on both sides, a self-free one is the cascade, exact because ranked.

idris.name: llog_2_5__hybrid_exact
idris.note: THE HYBRID IS EXACT: recomputing the recursive strata and keeping the refcount cascade on the self-free ones, in the SCC-DAG's order, yields exactly the global well-founded set whenever the well-founded facts are live, as at every boundary. The recompute can be confined to the recursive strata. No clause states this. The abstract model; the engine's step recomputes every stratum at once.

idris.name: llog_2_5__hybrid_mixed_after
idris.note: Executed: the seed withdrawn, the hybrid recomputes the recursive stratum to nothing and the cascade on the self-free stratum retracts 5 -- all three gone, as this clause requires.

idris.name: llog_2_5__hybrid_mixed_before
idris.note: Executed: with the seed, all four facts live under the hybrid.

idris.name: llog_2_5__hybrid_strata
idris.note: The witness strata: a recursive pair seeded by 10 below, a self-free 1 -> 5 above.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_base_in
idris.note: A base fact of the universe survives every stratum.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_compose
idris.note: N STRATA COMPOSE: the stratum-by-stratum recompute is the global one, both inclusions, for any number of strata. `llog_2_5__stratified_compose` is the two-strata case; this is the one the per-stratum mechanism runs.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_wf
idris.note: Recompute stratum by stratum: each stratum's well-founded set over the one below becomes the next stratum's base.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_mono_base_univ
idris.note: The well-founded set depends on the base only through its members in the universe.

idris.name: Llog_2_5__stratified
idris.note: Two strata of justifications in the SCC-DAG's order: the lower one never reads what the upper one derives.

idris.name: Llog_2_5__unfounded
idris.note: An unfounded set among a live set: nonempty, free of base facts, every justification keeping a member alive uses another member.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_unfounded
idris.note: What the refcount keeps beyond this clause's intended answer is an unfounded set, in general.

idris.name: iret_12_2__reach_refcount
idris.note: The refcount keeps both: recursion through a `logical` relation leaves unfounded facts live after the seed is withdrawn, which is why the recommendation ties `+recursive` to a TMS change.

idris.name: iret_12_2__witness_refcount
idris.note: After P is retracted the refcount of [IRET.12.2] keeps Q and R: each still has a justification, in the other. Read literally this clause is satisfied by that -- a justification remains -- and the fact is nevertheless unfounded. The clause means the well-founded reading, and [IRET.12.2] says so; the count is libds's mechanism on the acyclic support every admitted program has.

idris.name: iret_12_3__ranked_agree
idris.note: On a ranked support graph the refcount realises this clause exactly.

idris.name: llog_2_5__base_in_wf
idris.note: A base fact of the universe is well-founded.

idris.name: llog_2_5__compose_hb
idris.note: The composed recompute holds the base facts of the universe.

idris.name: llog_2_5__compose_hs
idris.note: And is closed under both strata's support.

idris.name: llog_2_5__compose_lower_in
idris.note: The lower stratum's recompute is within the global one.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_n
idris.note: n rounds.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_n_cons
idris.note: One more round at the front of a derivation, for witnesses against literal states.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_n_fixed
idris.note: From a known set that is a filter of the universe and that one round keeps, the derivation stabilises within as many rounds as the universe has facts beyond it: the fuel the derivation is given always suffices.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_n_stable
idris.note: Once a round adds nothing, no later round does.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_step
idris.note: One derivation round from what is known.

idris.name: llog_2_5__derive_step_mono
idris.note: One derivation round is monotone in what is known.

idris.name: llog_2_5__outside
idris.note: The facts outside a set; applied to the well-founded set, the candidate unfounded set.

idris.name: llog_2_5__reach_js
idris.note: The `+recursive` proposal's transitive-closure shape as justifications: seed -> Reach(a,b), Reach(a,b) + Edge(b,a) -> Reach(a,a), Reach(a,a) + Edge(a,b) -> Reach(a,b).

idris.name: llog_2_5__reach_well_founded
idris.note: Withdraw the seed, keep both edges: the well-founded answer retracts both Reach facts.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_after
idris.note: Executed: withdraw the seed and the global recompute keeps nothing.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_all
idris.note: The five-fact universe of the witness; small so the type-level evaluator finishes.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_before
idris.note: Executed and checked, as a chain of single-round `Refl`s: with the seed everything is well-founded.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_composed
idris.note: Executed: the two composed give the global recompute.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_js1
idris.note: Two-strata witness, lower stratum: a cycle seeded from outside it.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_js2
idris.note: Upper stratum: a second cycle seeded by the lower stratum's output.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_lower
idris.note: Executed: the lower stratum's recompute retracts its pair; its net diff is two retractions.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_upper
idris.note: Executed: the upper stratum, recomputed over the lower's output, retracts its pair although nothing of its own was withdrawn.

idris.name: llog_2_5__stratified_ante
idris.note: An antecedent of a lower-stratum justification that the composed recompute derives is derived by the lower stratum alone.

idris.name: llog_2_5__stratified_compose
idris.note: Stratified recomputation composes: the least fixpoint of two strata together is the least fixpoint of the upper over the lower's. Recompute-and-diff can run stratum by stratum in the DAG's order.

idris.name: llog_2_5__unfounded_disagrees
idris.note: Conversely an unfounded set among the survivors is disjoint from the well-founded set. With `iret_12_2__cascade_unfounded`: the refcount and this clause's intended answer agree exactly when the survivors hold no unfounded set -- the characterisation the module's header claimed and now proves.

idris.name: llog_2_5__unfounded_hb
idris.note: The well-founded facts outside an unfounded set hold the base facts of the universe.

idris.name: llog_2_5__unfounded_hs
idris.note: And are closed under support.

idris.name: llog_2_5__well_founded
idris.note: The least fixpoint of support: what remains after the last justification goes away, with "justification" read as one grounded in base facts.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_closed
idris.note: A fact of the universe supported by well-founded facts is well-founded.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_fixed
idris.note: The well-founded set is a fixpoint of derivation.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_in_cascade
idris.note: The cascade never retracts a well-founded fact.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_least
idris.note: The well-founded set is below every closed set, so it is the LEAST fixpoint: this clause's "last justification" read as the last GROUNDED one, which is the reading the TMS change proposes.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_mono_base
idris.note: Fewer base facts, no more well-founded facts: a withdrawal of inputs only ever retracts derived facts, so recompute-and-diff commits retractions only.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_sub_all
idris.note: The well-founded set lies in the universe.

idris.name: llog_2_5__witness_before
idris.note: Before P is retracted everything is live and well-founded.

idris.name: llog_2_5__witness_js
idris.note: P -> Q, Q -> R, R -> Q as justifications, with P the one base fact.

idris.name: llog_2_5__witness_well_founded
idris.note: After P is retracted the well-founded answer retracts Q and R: their last grounded justification is gone.
